notes.estimator_accuracy_warning: BOUNDED CLAIM - preserve verbatim, do not simplify. This run's declared total understates its own cost by a factor it directly measured against itself (senior 14241 declared vs 37636 measured = 2.64x; security 13812 vs 28042 = 2.03x). The sibling's declared total was NEVER independently measured, so its true undercount is unknown - only that it appears smaller, since its declared review-phase tokens (30699, 30873) already sit near this run's measured consumption. Scaling this run's two review phases to measured tokens, holding the declared in/out mix, replaces $0.277045 with $0.649616 (+$0.372571) for an adjusted total near $1.036, roughly +62% over the sibling's declared $0.638539. That $1.036 figure is a SCENARIO, not a corrected total: it is built by holding one run's ratio constant and applying it without ever measuring the sibling the same way. It must not be reported as 'this run is secretly 62% more expensive.' Raw declared-vs-declared is $0.663891 vs $0.638539 (+4%), which on n=1 is not meaningful on its own either.

notes.quality_attribution: MOST IMPORTANT FINDING - must not be subordinated to the cost discussion. This run made 1 write attempt with 0 refinement packets and passed all three falsifiability traps first time; the sibling made 2 write attempts, having fallen into the FT-1 'chips show selected values' trap and corrected it only after review. The cause is WHERE THE TRAP WAS CAUGHT, not model or policy strength: the operator handed this run the trap pre-solved, and it was written into requirements.md section 5 before any codegen. The sibling had to discover FT-1 through review. Any reader who takes '1 write attempt vs 2' as a policy quality signal without this attribution is drawing a conclusion the data does not support. The two runs are confounded in both directions and are not directly comparable on either axis: the cost comparison compares different amounts of work (the sibling paid for a correction this run did not; this run paid a premium tier for an edit the sibling's mechanical tier produced).
notes.review_specification_property: Both runs' security reviewers independently recorded 'npm audit' as NOT RUN rather than a false 'pass' when no dependency delta existed to audit. Two independent instances of the same correct behavior is evidence of a property of how these reviews are specified, not a coincidence.
